answer_1.quote: The core idea behind the annotation-based evaluation method proposed by  is that instead of assigning overall scores to each sentence, 2 or classifying each error into a predefined error scheme, evaluators mark up word spans in translated texts that contain given types of errors.

answer_4.quote: In both studies, each translated review was annotated by two evaluators.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to mark up translations first for Comprehensibility, then for Adequacy, distinguishing two levels of severity for each: major errors (incomprehensible/not conveying the meaning of the source) and minor errors (difficult to understand due to grammar or stylistic errors/not an optimal translation choice for the given source).
